He attributed the denial to "the messengers," although they only denied the one messenger sent to them, because whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers, since every messenger commands belief in the others. It is also said that they denied Noah in his prophethood, and denied him regarding what he told them of the coming of messengers after him.

﴿When their brother Noah said to them﴾: that is, their brother by descent, not a brother in religion.

It is said that this is brotherhood of kinship (أخوة المجانسة). It is also said that it comes from the Arab usage "O brother of Banu Tamim," meaning one of them.

﴿Will you not fear (God)?﴾: that is, will you not fear God by abandoning the worship of idols and responding to His messenger whom He sent to you.

﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾: that is, I am a messenger from God, trustworthy in what I convey from Him. It is also said: trustworthy among you, for they had known his trustworthiness and truthfulness.

﴿So fear God and obey me﴾: that is, make obedience to God a protection for yourselves from His punishment, (p. 1062) and obey me in what I command you from God: belief in Him, abandoning polytheism, and performing the obligations of the religion.

﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾: that is, I do not seek from you any wage for conveying the message, nor do I hope for that from you. ﴿My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾: the reward I seek and desire is only with Him, that is, I expect my recompense only from Him. He repeated "So fear God and obey me" for emphasis and to fix it in their souls, although He linked each of them to a cause: trustworthiness in the first, and cutting off the expectation of wages in the second. A parallel to this is your saying: "Will you not fear God in disobeying me, when I raised you as a child? Will you not fear God in disobeying me, when I taught you as an adult?" The command to fear God was mentioned before the command to obey Him, because fearing God is the cause of obeying Him.

﴿They said: "Shall we believe you, when the lowest have followed you?"﴾: the interrogative is for denial, meaning: how can we follow you and believe you, when the lowest have already followed you? The word (أرذل) is plural of (أرذل), its broken plural is (أرذال), and its feminine is (رُذلى). They are the least in standing and wealth. Rudhalah means lowliness and abasement. They regarded them as contemptible because of the smallness of their wealth and standing, or because their lineages were not preserved.

It is also said that they were people of lowly crafts. The explanation of these verses has already been given in (Surah) Hud.

Ibn Mas'ud, al-Dahhak, and Ya'qub al-Hadrami read ﴿and those who follow you are the lowest﴾ (واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ) with a conjunction. Al-Nahhas said: this is a good reading, because this (و) is often followed by nouns, and (أتباع) is the plural of (تابع, follower).

Noah answered them with his words: ﴿And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?﴾ Here (كانَ) is redundant (زائدة), and the meaning is: what is my knowledge of their knowledge? That is, I was not charged with knowing their deeds. I was only charged with calling them to belief and to reflection upon it, not to judge by trades, crafts, poverty, or wealth. It seems that by their words "the lowest have followed you" they were pointing out that their belief was not based on sound reflection, so he answered them with this. It is also said that the meaning is: I did not know that God would guide them and leave you astray.

﴿Their account is only upon my Lord, if you were aware﴾: that is, their reckoning and the searching into their inner thoughts and deeds is only upon God, if you were people of perception and understanding. The majority read (تشعرون) with the second-person (فوقية, "you"). Ibn Abi 'Abla, Ibn al-Sumayfa', al-A'raj, and Abu Zur'ah read it with the third-person (تحتية, "they"), as if he had left addressing the disbelievers and turned to speaking about them.

Al-Zajjaj said: crafts do not harm one in matters of religion.

How excellent is His saying: ﴿I am not one to drive away the believers﴾. This is Noah's answer to what appeared in their speech of their demand that he drive them away.

﴿I am only a clear warner﴾: that is, I am only a warner who clarifies what God, glorified is He, commanded me to convey to you. This sentence serves as the reason for what precedes it.

﴿They said: "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned."﴾: that is, if you do not stop reviling our religion and insulting our gods, you will surely be among those stoned with rocks. It is also said: among those reviled, and it is said: among those killed. After that exchange between them and Noah, they turned to arrogance and threats.

When Noah heard their words, ﴿he said: "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me."﴾: that is, they persisted in denying me, and did not hear my words nor respond to my call.

﴿So judge between me and them with a judgment﴾: al-fath (الفتح) means judgment. That is: decide between me and them with a decision. The true meaning of al-fath has already been discussed.

﴿And save me and those with me of the believers.﴾ When he called upon his Lord with this supplication, He answered him, saying: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship﴾: that is, the filled ship. Al-shahn (الشحن) is the filling of the ship with people, animals, and goods.

﴿Then We drowned the remaining ones afterward﴾: that is, after saving them, We drowned the rest of his people.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾: a great sign and lesson. ﴿But most of them were not believers.﴾ Here (كان) is redundant according to Sibawayh and others, as has already been explained.

﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾: that is, the Subduer of His enemies, the Merciful to His allies.

﴿'Ad denied the messengers﴾: he made the verb feminine by considering its attribution to the tribe, since 'Ad is the name of their highest forefather.

The meaning of their denying the messengers, though they denied only one messenger, has already been explained earlier in the story of Noah.

﴿When their brother Hud said to them: "Will you not fear God?"﴾: the discussion of this is like the discussion of Noah's words above.

Likewise His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear God and obey me. And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾: the discussion of this is exactly the same as the preceding.

﴿Do you build on every elevated place a landmark, sporting?﴾ Al-ri' (الريع) is an elevated place of land, plural of (ريعة). One says: "How high (كم) is the ri' of your land?" meaning: how high is it?

Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-ri' is height, plural of (ريعة). Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and al-Kalbi said: al-ri' is a road. Muqatil and al-Suddi also said this. The application of al-ri' to what is raised from the earth is well known among lexicographers, and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

*Its flight-feathers are spread, rising above a ri'a,*
*in the dark of night, shimmering in its plumage.*

It is also said that al-ri' is a mountain, its singular being (ريعة), and its plural (أرياع).

Mujahid said: it is a pass between two mountains. It is narrated from him that it is a small hill pass, and also narrated from him that it is a lookout.

The meaning of the verse is: you build at every elevated place a landmark, playing with its construction, mocking passersby and ridiculing them, because you look down from that high building onto the road, harming passersby and mocking them.

Al-Kalbi said: it is the sport of tax-collectors with the wealth of those who pass by them, as related by al-Mawardi.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-ri' is a monastery tower; al-ri' is a tower that stands in the desert; al-ri' is a high hill. There are two dialects for (ri'): with a kasra on the ra' and with a fatha.

﴿And you take for yourselves fortresses﴾: al-masani' (المصانع) are the buildings that people take as residences.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: every building constructed is a masna'ah. Al-Kalbi and others said the same. From it is the poet's saying:

*They left their dwellings for them as wastelands,*
*and they demolished the masani' and the towers.*

It is also said that they are strong fortresses, as Mujahid and others said. Al-Zajjaj said: they are water reservoirs made beneath the ground, whose singular is (مصنعة) and (مصنع). From it is the saying of Labid:

*and the mountains and the masani' remain after us.*

There is nothing in this verse that clearly indicates what al-Zajjaj said. However, al-Jawhari said: al-masna'ah with a damma on the nun is a basin in which rainwater is gathered, and al-masani' are fortresses.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-masani', in our dialect of Yemen, are high palaces.

The meaning of ﴿so that you may abide forever﴾ is: hoping that you will live forever. It is also said that la'alla here is interrogative of reproach: that is, do you abide forever? Like their saying "perhaps you will insult me," meaning: will you insult me? (p. 1063)

Al-Farra' said: "in order that you may abide forever, and not reflect on death." It is also said that the meaning is: as if you were eternal and everlasting.

The majority read (تخلدون) with a light pronunciation. Qatadah read it with a shadda. Al-Nahhas reported that in some readings it is "as if you were everlasting" (كأنّكم مُخَلَّدُون). Ibn Mas'ud read (كي تخلدوا).

﴿And when you seize (by force), you seize as tyrants﴾: al-batsh (البطش) is domination and taking by violence.

Mujahid and others said: al-batsh is harsh oppression, killing by the sword and striking with the whip.

It is said: the intended meaning is "And when you intend to seize," so that the condition and the response are not identical. Jabbarin (جبارين) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state.

Al-Zajjaj said: he only denounced them for this because it is injustice; but in what is right, striking with the whip or the sword is permissible.

He attributed the denial to "the messengers," although they only denied the one messenger sent to them, because whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers, since every messenger commands belief in the others. It is also said that they denied Noah in his prophethood, and denied him regarding what he told them of the coming of messengers after him.

﴿When their brother Noah said to them﴾: that is, their brother by descent, not a brother in religion.

It is said that this is brotherhood of kinship (أخوة المجانسة). It is also said that it comes from the Arab usage "O brother of Banu Tamim," meaning one of them.

﴿Will you not fear (God)?﴾: that is, will you not fear God by abandoning the worship of idols and responding to His messenger whom He sent to you.

﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾: that is, I am a messenger from God, trustworthy in what I convey from Him. It is also said: trustworthy among you, for they had known his trustworthiness and truthfulness.

﴿So fear God and obey me﴾: that is, make obedience to God a protection for yourselves from His punishment, (p. 1062) and obey me in what I command you from God: belief in Him, abandoning polytheism, and performing the obligations of the religion.

﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾: that is, I do not seek from you any wage for conveying the message, nor do I hope for that from you. ﴿My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾: the reward I seek and desire is only with Him, that is, I expect my recompense only from Him. He repeated "So fear God and obey me" for emphasis and to fix it in their souls, although He linked each of them to a cause: trustworthiness in the first, and cutting off the expectation of wages in the second. A parallel to this is your saying: "Will you not fear God in disobeying me, when I raised you as a child? Will you not fear God in disobeying me, when I taught you as an adult?" The command to fear God was mentioned before the command to obey Him, because fearing God is the cause of obeying Him.

﴿They said: "Shall we believe you, when the lowest have followed you?"﴾: the interrogative is for denial, meaning: how can we follow you and believe you, when the lowest have already followed you? The word (أرذل) is plural of (أرذل), its broken plural is (أرذال), and its feminine is (رُذلى). They are the least in standing and wealth. Rudhalah means lowliness and abasement. They regarded them as contemptible because of the smallness of their wealth and standing, or because their lineages were not preserved.

It is also said that they were people of lowly crafts. The explanation of these verses has already been given in (Surah) Hud.

Ibn Mas'ud, al-Dahhak, and Ya'qub al-Hadrami read ﴿and those who follow you are the lowest﴾ (واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ) with a conjunction. Al-Nahhas said: this is a good reading, because this (و) is often followed by nouns, and (أتباع) is the plural of (تابع, follower).

Noah answered them with his words: ﴿And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?﴾ Here (كانَ) is redundant (زائدة), and the meaning is: what is my knowledge of their knowledge? That is, I was not charged with knowing their deeds. I was only charged with calling them to belief and to reflection upon it, not to judge by trades, crafts, poverty, or wealth. It seems that by their words "the lowest have followed you" they were pointing out that their belief was not based on sound reflection, so he answered them with this. It is also said that the meaning is: I did not know that God would guide them and leave you astray.

﴿Their account is only upon my Lord, if you were aware﴾: that is, their reckoning and the searching into their inner thoughts and deeds is only upon God, if you were people of perception and understanding. The majority read (تشعرون) with the second-person (فوقية, "you"). Ibn Abi 'Abla, Ibn al-Sumayfa', al-A'raj, and Abu Zur'ah read it with the third-person (تحتية, "they"), as if he had left addressing the disbelievers and turned to speaking about them.

Al-Zajjaj said: crafts do not harm one in matters of religion.

How excellent is His saying: ﴿I am not one to drive away the believers﴾. This is Noah's answer to what appeared in their speech of their demand that he drive them away.

﴿I am only a clear warner﴾: that is, I am only a warner who clarifies what God, glorified is He, commanded me to convey to you. This sentence serves as the reason for what precedes it.

﴿They said: "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned."﴾: that is, if you do not stop reviling our religion and insulting our gods, you will surely be among those stoned with rocks. It is also said: among those reviled, and it is said: among those killed. After that exchange between them and Noah, they turned to arrogance and threats.

When Noah heard their words, ﴿he said: "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me."﴾: that is, they persisted in denying me, and did not hear my words nor respond to my call.

﴿So judge between me and them with a judgment﴾: al-fath (الفتح) means judgment. That is: decide between me and them with a decision. The true meaning of al-fath has already been discussed.

﴿And save me and those with me of the believers.﴾ When he called upon his Lord with this supplication, He answered him, saying: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship﴾: that is, the filled ship. Al-shahn (الشحن) is the filling of the ship with people, animals, and goods.

﴿Then We drowned the remaining ones afterward﴾: that is, after saving them, We drowned the rest of his people.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾: a great sign and lesson. ﴿But most of them were not believers.﴾ Here (كان) is redundant according to Sibawayh and others, as has already been explained.

﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾: that is, the Subduer of His enemies, the Merciful to His allies.

﴿'Ad denied the messengers﴾: he made the verb feminine by considering its attribution to the tribe, since 'Ad is the name of their highest forefather.

The meaning of their denying the messengers, though they denied only one messenger, has already been explained earlier in the story of Noah.

﴿When their brother Hud said to them: "Will you not fear God?"﴾: the discussion of this is like the discussion of Noah's words above.

Likewise His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear God and obey me. And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾: the discussion of this is exactly the same as the preceding.

﴿Do you build on every elevated place a landmark, sporting?﴾ Al-ri' (الريع) is an elevated place of land, plural of (ريعة). One says: "How high (كم) is the ri' of your land?" meaning: how high is it?

Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-ri' is height, plural of (ريعة). Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and al-Kalbi said: al-ri' is a road. Muqatil and al-Suddi also said this. The application of al-ri' to what is raised from the earth is well known among lexicographers, and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

*Its flight-feathers are spread, rising above a ri'a,*
*in the dark of night, shimmering in its plumage.*

It is also said that al-ri' is a mountain, its singular being (ريعة), and its plural (أرياع).

Mujahid said: it is a pass between two mountains. It is narrated from him that it is a small hill pass, and also narrated from him that it is a lookout.

The meaning of the verse is: you build at every elevated place a landmark, playing with its construction, mocking passersby and ridiculing them, because you look down from that high building onto the road, harming passersby and mocking them.

Al-Kalbi said: it is the sport of tax-collectors with the wealth of those who pass by them, as related by al-Mawardi.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-ri' is a monastery tower; al-ri' is a tower that stands in the desert; al-ri' is a high hill. There are two dialects for (ri'): with a kasra on the ra' and with a fatha.

﴿And you take for yourselves fortresses﴾: al-masani' (المصانع) are the buildings that people take as residences.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: every building constructed is a masna'ah. Al-Kalbi and others said the same. From it is the poet's saying:

*They left their dwellings for them as wastelands,*
*and they demolished the masani' and the towers.*

It is also said that they are strong fortresses, as Mujahid and others said. Al-Zajjaj said: they are water reservoirs made beneath the ground, whose singular is (مصنعة) and (مصنع). From it is the saying of Labid:

*and the mountains and the masani' remain after us.*

There is nothing in this verse that clearly indicates what al-Zajjaj said. However, al-Jawhari said: al-masna'ah with a damma on the nun is a basin in which rainwater is gathered, and al-masani' are fortresses.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-masani', in our dialect of Yemen, are high palaces.

The meaning of ﴿so that you may abide forever﴾ is: hoping that you will live forever. It is also said that la'alla here is interrogative of reproach: that is, do you abide forever? Like their saying "perhaps you will insult me," meaning: will you insult me? (p. 1063)

Al-Farra' said: "in order that you may abide forever, and not reflect on death." It is also said that the meaning is: as if you were eternal and everlasting.

The majority read (تخلدون) with a light pronunciation. Qatadah read it with a shadda. Al-Nahhas reported that in some readings it is "as if you were everlasting" (كأنّكم مُخَلَّدُون). Ibn Mas'ud read (كي تخلدوا).

﴿And when you seize (by force), you seize as tyrants﴾: al-batsh (البطش) is domination and taking by violence.

Mujahid and others said: al-batsh is harsh oppression, killing by the sword and striking with the whip.

It is said: the intended meaning is "And when you intend to seize," so that the condition and the response are not identical. Jabbarin (جبارين) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state.

Al-Zajjaj said: he only denounced them for this because it is injustice; but in what is right, striking with the whip or the sword is permissible.

﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾: that is, the Subduer of His enemies, the Merciful to His allies.

﴿'Ad denied the messengers﴾: he made the verb feminine by considering its attribution to the tribe, since 'Ad is the name of their highest forefather.

The meaning of their denying the messengers, though they denied only one messenger, has already been explained earlier in the story of Noah.

﴿When their brother Hud said to them: "Will you not fear God?"﴾: the discussion of this is like the discussion of Noah's words above.

Likewise His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear God and obey me. And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾: the discussion of this is exactly the same as the preceding.

﴿Do you build on every elevated place a landmark, sporting?﴾ Al-ri' (الريع) is an elevated place of land, plural of (ريعة). One says: "How high (كم) is the ri' of your land?" meaning: how high is it?

Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-ri' is height, plural of (ريعة). Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and al-Kalbi said: al-ri' is a road. Muqatil and al-Suddi also said this. The application of al-ri' to what is raised from the earth is well known among lexicographers, and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

*Its flight-feathers are spread, rising above a ri'a,*
*in the dark of night, shimmering in its plumage.*

It is also said that al-ri' is a mountain, its singular being (ريعة), and its plural (أرياع).

Mujahid said: it is a pass between two mountains. It is narrated from him that it is a small hill pass, and also narrated from him that it is a lookout.

The meaning of the verse is: you build at every elevated place a landmark, playing with its construction, mocking passersby and ridiculing them, because you look down from that high building onto the road, harming passersby and mocking them.

Al-Kalbi said: it is the sport of tax-collectors with the wealth of those who pass by them, as related by al-Mawardi.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-ri' is a monastery tower; al-ri' is a tower that stands in the desert; al-ri' is a high hill. There are two dialects for (ri'): with a kasra on the ra' and with a fatha.

﴿And you take for yourselves fortresses﴾: al-masani' (المصانع) are the buildings that people take as residences.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: every building constructed is a masna'ah. Al-Kalbi and others said the same. From it is the poet's saying:

*They left their dwellings for them as wastelands,*
*and they demolished the masani' and the towers.*

It is also said that they are strong fortresses, as Mujahid and others said. Al-Zajjaj said: they are water reservoirs made beneath the ground, whose singular is (مصنعة) and (مصنع). From it is the saying of Labid:

*We were worn out, yet the lasting stars are not worn,*
*and the mountains and the masani' remain after us.*

There is nothing in this verse that clearly indicates what al-Zajjaj said. However, al-Jawhari said: al-masna'ah with a damma on the nun is a basin in which rainwater is gathered, and al-masani' are fortresses.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-masani', in our dialect of Yemen, are high palaces.

The meaning of ﴿so that you may abide forever﴾ is: hoping that you will live forever. It is also said that la'alla here is interrogative of reproach: that is, do you abide forever? Like their saying "perhaps you will insult me," meaning: will you insult me? (p. 1063)

Al-Farra' said: "in order that you may abide forever, and not reflect on death." It is also said that the meaning is: as if you were eternal and everlasting.

The majority read (تخلدون) with a light pronunciation. Qatadah read it with a shadda. Al-Nahhas reported that in some readings it is "as if you were everlasting" (كأنّكم مُخَلَّدُون). Ibn Mas'ud read (كي تخلدوا).

﴿And when you seize (by force), you seize as tyrants﴾: al-batsh (البطش) is domination and taking by violence.

Mujahid and others said: al-batsh is harsh oppression, killing by the sword and striking with the whip.

The meaning is: you did that unjustly. It is also said: it is killing in anger, as al-Hasan and al-Kalbi said. It is said: the intended meaning is "And when you intend to seize," so that the condition and the response are not identical. Jabbarin (جبارين) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state.

Al-Zajjaj said: he only denounced them for this because it is injustice; but in what is right, striking with the whip or the sword is permissible.

Then, when He described them with these ugly attributes, indicating injustice, arrogance, rebellion, and tyranny, He commanded them to be mindful of God.

﴿So fear God and obey me﴾: he stated fear of God in general, then detailed it in His saying: ﴿And fear Him who has provided you with what you know﴾. ﴿He provided you with livestock and children﴾, and he repeated the verb for emphasis and confirmation.

﴿And gardens and springs﴾: that is, orchards, rivers, and wells.

Then he admonished and warned them, saying: ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day﴾ if you disbelieve, persist in what you are upon, and do not give thanks for these blessings. By the great punishment is meant both the punishment of this world and that of the Hereafter.

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿They said: "Shall we believe you?"﴾: that is, shall we confirm you?

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and those who follow you are the lowest﴾: he said: the weavers (الحواكون).

He also reported from Qatadah, who said: the base and lowest of people.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿the laden ship﴾: he said: the filled.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him that he said: "Do you know what al-mashhun is?" We said: "No." He said: it is the loaded.

Ibn Jarir also reported from him: it is the burdened.

Ibn Jarir also reported from him regarding ﴿on every ri'﴾: he said: a road. ﴿A landmark﴾: he said: a sign. ﴿You play﴾: he said: you sport.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also reported from him regarding ﴿on every ri'﴾: he said: a height.

They also reported from him regarding ﴿so that you may abide forever﴾: he said: as if you were to abide forever.

Ibn Abi Hatim also reported from him regarding ﴿jabbarin﴾: he said: strong.

Meaning: your admonition and your not admonishing are the same to us; we do not care about any of it and pay no heed to what you say.

Al-ʿAbbās narrated from Abū ʿAmr, and Bishr narrated from al-Kisāʾī, "Awʿaẓta" (أوَعَظْتَ) with the ẓāʾ assimilated into the tāʾ (idghām). This is weak, because the letter ẓāʾ is an emphatic (ʾiṭbāq) letter, and assimilation occurs only into a letter very close to it.

This reading is also attributed to ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ibn Muḥaysin. The rest of the readers recited with the ẓāʾ made clear (iẓhār).

﴿This is nothing but the custom of the ancients.﴾ That is: what you have brought us and called us to of religion is nothing but the custom of the ancients, i.e., the practice they followed.

It has also been said: the meaning is, what you have brought us and called us to of religion is nothing but the custom of the ancients and their practice. This is based on what al-Farrāʾ and others said: that the meaning of ﴿khuluq al-awwalīn﴾ is ʿādat al-awwalīn (the custom of the ancients). Al-Naḥḥās said: "Khuluq al-awwalīn," according to al-Farrāʾ, means ʿādat al-awwalīn.

Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, who said: ﴿khuluq al-awwalīn﴾ means their way and what their affairs followed, and the two statements are close in meaning.

He said: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd also related to us that the meaning of ﴿khuluq al-awwalīn﴾ is their falsehood (takdhībuhum).

Muqātil said: they said, "What you call us to is nothing but the lies of the ancients."

Al-Wāḥidī said: this is also the view of Ibn Masʿūd and Mujāhid.

He said: al-khuluq and al-ikhtilāq mean lying, and from it is His saying: ﴿and you invent a lie (takhluqūna ifkan)﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 17]. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Yaʿqūb read "khalq al-awwalīn" with a fatḥah on the khāʾ and sukūn on the lām.

The rest read with a ḍammah on both the khāʾ and the lām.

Al-Harawī said: its meaning according to the first reading is their fabrication and their lying; according to the second reading, their custom. This distinction is necessary.

Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: al-khuluq is religion, al-khuluq is natural disposition, and al-khuluq is manliness/chivalry. Abū Qilāba read with a ḍammah on the khāʾ and sukūn on the lām, and this is a lightened form of the ḍammah reading for both. The apparent meaning of the verse is the statement of those who said: "What we are upon is nothing but the custom and practice of the ancients." This is supported by their saying: ﴿and we are not going to be punished﴾, i.e., for what we do of violence and the like, which we are upon now.

﴿So they denied him, and We destroyed them﴾, i.e., by the wind, as the Qurʾān stated explicitly in other places. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed your Lord — He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ The explanation of this has already preceded in this surah.

Then, when He — glorified is He — finished mentioning the story of Hūd and his people, He mentioned the story of Ṣāliḥ and his people. They used to dwell in al-Ḥijr, so He said: ﴿Thamūd denied the messengers﴾ up to His saying ﴿except upon the Lord of the worlds﴾. Its explanation has already preceded in the story of Hūd mentioned before this story.

﴿Will you be left in what is here, secure?﴾ The interrogative is for denunciation, i.e., will you be left, in these blessings Allah has given you, secure from death and punishment, remaining in this world? And since He had left the blessings vague here, He explained them with His saying: ﴿in gardens and springs﴾ ﴿and fields and palm trees whose fruit-stalks are delicate (haḍīm)﴾. Al-Haḍīm is the ripe, soft, tender, fine. Al-ṭalʿ is what emerges from the fruit. He mentioned the palm trees along with their being included under the gardens because of their excellence over the rest of the trees. They often mention a single thing with a word that encompasses it and other things, just as they mention "camels" among the blessings while intending only camels; and likewise they mention "the garden" while intending only the palm trees. Zuhayr said:

"As if my two eyes, in my water-skin, were a sprinkled (muqattalah) pair of water-carrying camels watering a garden of tall palms (suḥuqan)."

Suḥuqan is the plural of saḥūq, and it is only applied to palm trees. It has been said: the gardens refers to trees other than palms, but the first is preferable. Al-Māwardī related twelve opinions on the meaning of haḍīm, the best of which and the most consistent with the language is what we have mentioned.

﴿And you hew houses out of the mountains, skillfully (fārihīn)﴾. Al-naḥt is carving and shaving; naḥata yanḥituhu (with kasra) means he shaped it; al-niḥātah is shavings. They used to carve their houses out of the mountains when their lifespans were long and their buildings made of clay had collapsed.

Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Dhakwān read "fārihīn" (fārihīn) without an alif; the rest read "fārihīn" with the alif.

Abū ʿUbayda and others said: the two have one meaning.

Al-farah means vigor, and Abū ʿUbayd and others distinguished between them, saying: fārihīn means skilled at carving them; it was also said: domineering (mutajabbirīn); and "farihīn" means exultant, insolent, and this is what Mujāhid and others said.

It was said: greedy (shariḥīn); al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: clever (kayyisīn); Qatādah said: proud, pleased, secure (āminīn), and al-Ḥasan said likewise; it was said: joyful, said by al-Akhfash; Ibn Zayd said: strong.

﴿So fear Allah and obey me, and do not obey the command of the extravagant﴾, i.e., the polytheists; it was also said: those who hamstrung the she-camel. Then He described these extravagant ones with His saying: ﴿who cause corruption in the land and do not reform﴾, i.e., that is their habit: they commit corruption in the land and no righteousness proceeds from them at all.

﴿They said, "You are only of those bewitched (musaḥḥarīn)."﴾ That is, those who have been afflicted by magic, said by Mujāhid and Qatādah. It was also said: the musaḥḥar is the one who is sustained by food and drink, said by al-Kalbī and others; so the musaḥḥar is one who has a saḥr, which is the lung. It is as if they said: "You are only a human like us, eating and drinking."

Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e., you eat food and drink and are nourished by it. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays or Labīd:

"If you ask us what we are, we are sparrows of these bewitched (musaḥḥar) creatures."

Imru' al-Qays also said:

"We see ourselves as two places for a fated unseen, and we are nourished by food and by drink."

Al-Mu'arrij said: al-musaḥḥar is the created one, in the dialect of Rabīʿah.

﴿You are only a human like us; so bring a sign, if you are of the truthful﴾ in your saying and claim.

﴿He said, "This is a she-camel; for her is a drink, and for you is a drink of a known day."﴾ That is: for her is a share of the water, and for you is a known share of it; it is not for you to drink on the day that is her share, nor does she drink on the day that is your share.

Al-Farrāʾ said: al-shirb is the portion of water.

Al-Naḥḥās said: as for the verbal noun, it is said shariba shurban, most of them with ḍammah; al-shirb with a fatḥah on the shīn is the plural of shārib; here what is meant is al-shirb with a kasra, and this is how the majority read both; Ibn Abī ʿAbla read both with a ḍammah.

﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ That is: do not touch her by hamstringing, striking, or anything that would harm her. The answer to the prohibition is ﴿fa-yaʾkhudhakum﴾ (lest there seize you).

﴿So they hamstrung her, and then they became regretful﴾ over her hamstringing, when they knew that the punishment was descending upon them. That was because He gave them respite for three days, and the sign appeared on them each day; they regretted when regret was of no benefit, for it does not avail at the sight of punishment and the appearance of its signs.

﴿So the punishment seized them﴾ which He had promised them.

The explanation of His saying ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾ and ﴿And indeed your Lord — He is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ has preceded in this surah, and the explanation of the story of Ṣāliḥ and his people has also preceded in other surahs.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from him that he said: "ayna'a wa-balagh" (it ripened and reached maturity). Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from him also that he said: "arṭaba wa-istarkhā" (it became dates and became soft). Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from him also regarding His saying ﴿fārihīn﴾ that he said: "ḥādhiqīn" (skilled). Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from him that he said: "fārihīn" means "ashirīn" (insolent). Al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Mujāhid that he said: "shariḥīn" (greedy).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Khaṭīb and Ibn ʿAsākir related through several chains from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying ﴿You are only of the musaḥḥarīn﴾ that he said: "of the created ones (makhlūqīn)," and recited the verse of Labīd ibn Rabīʿah:

"If you ask us what we are..." [the full verse]

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd also related from him regarding His saying ﴿for her is a drink﴾ that he said: "When it is her day, she would yield milk for them, however much they wished."

Meaning: your admonition and your not admonishing are the same to us; we do not care about any of it and pay no heed to what you say.

﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses﴾, that is, you abandon what Allah has created for your enjoyment of it among the women. By "spouses" He means the female sex in general. ﴿Rather, you are a people transgressing﴾, that is, exceeding the limit in all acts of disobedience, and this act you commit with males is among them.

*"So I am not one whose companionship is hated, nor one who hates."*

And another said:

Al-Nahhas said: *ghābir* is said of the one who departs and of the one who remains.

*"Do not whip the she-camels' udders with their remaining milk, for you do not know who will be the one who gives birth."*

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾, that is, We destroyed them by sinking and by stoning.

﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾, meaning stones, ﴿so evil was the rain of the warned.﴾ The thing praised or condemned is omitted, and the sense is "their rain."

The explanation of this has already passed in the surah of Subhan (al-Isra'). It has been read as *bi-l-qusṭās* with a ḍamma and also with a kasra.

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related the same from Ikrima.

Ishaq ibn Bishr and Ibn Asakir related from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿The companions of the thicket denied the messengers﴾, that he said: "They were the companions of a thicket on the shore of the sea, extending to Madyan." ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them﴾, and he did not say "their brother Shu'ayb," because he was not of their kind. ﴿Will you not fear Allah?﴾ How can you not fear Him, when you know that I am a trustworthy messenger? Will you not take heed from the destruction of Madyan, who were destroyed for what they used to do? The companions of the thicket, despite what they were in of polytheism, followed the custom of the companions of Madyan. So Shu'ayb said to them: "Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. I do not ask you for any reward for what I call you to in this world from your wealth. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds. And fear Him who created you and the former generations," meaning the earlier generations who were destroyed for their sins, "and do not perish like them." ﴿They said, "You are only of those bewitched"﴾, meaning of the created beings. ﴿And you are not but a human like us, and indeed we think you are among the liars. So cause to fall upon us fragments from the sky﴾, meaning pieces from the sky. ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them.﴾ Allah sent against them scorching winds from Hell, and they surrounded them for seven days until the heat cooked them. Their houses became hot, and their water boiled in the wells and springs. So they left their dwellings and their settlements, fleeing, and the scorching wind was with them. Allah then made the sun dominant over them from above their heads, and it covered them until their skulls rattled within it. And Allah made the hot sand dominant beneath their feet until the flesh of their feet fell away. Then a shade like a black cloud arose for them. When they saw it, they rushed to seek refuge in its shade. When all of them were gathered beneath it, it closed over them, and they perished. Allah saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him, saying concerning ﴿and the former generations﴾: "the earlier creations."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim also related from him that he was asked about His saying ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them.﴾ He said: "Allah sent upon them an intense heat that seized their breaths, so they entered the inner parts of the houses, but it entered upon them within the houses and seized their souls. So they came out of the houses fleeing into the wilderness. Then Allah sent upon them a cloud that shaded them from the sun, and they found in it coolness and pleasure. So they called to one another until, when they had gathered beneath it, Allah rained fire upon them. That is the punishment of the Day of the Shade."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim also related from him: "Whoever relates to you from the scholars the punishment of the Day of the Shade, then deny him."

I say: What can we say concerning what he (may Allah be pleased with him) related to us of that, which we have transmitted from him here? It may be said that since he was the sea whom Allah taught the interpretation of His Book through the supplication of His Prophet (may Allah bless him, his family and grant him peace), he was singled out for knowledge of this report apart from other scholars. So whoever relates the report of the punishment of the Shade in a manner other than this manner which he related to us, then he has enjoined us to deny him, because he knew it and no one else knew it.

Allah then made the sun dominant over them from above their heads, and it covered them until their skulls rattled within it. And Allah made the hot sand dominant beneath their feet until the flesh of their feet fell away. Then a shade like a black cloud arose for them. When they saw it, they rushed to seek refuge in its shade. When all of them were gathered beneath it, it closed over them, and they perished. Allah saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him, saying concerning ﴿and the former generations﴾: "the earlier creations."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim also related from him that he was asked about His saying ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them.﴾ He said: "Allah sent upon them an intense heat that seized their breaths, so they entered the inner parts of the houses, but it entered upon them within the houses and seized their souls. So they came out of the houses fleeing into the wilderness. Then Allah sent upon them a cloud that shaded them from the sun, and they found in it coolness and pleasure. So they called to one another until, when they had gathered beneath it, Allah rained fire upon them. That is the punishment of the Day of the Shade."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim also related from him: "Whoever relates to you from the scholars the punishment of the Day of the Shade, then deny him."

I say: What can we say concerning what he (may Allah be pleased with him) related to us of that, which we have transmitted from him here? It may be said that since he was the sea whom Allah taught the interpretation of His Book through the supplication of His Prophet (may Allah bless him, his family and grant him peace), he was singled out for knowledge of this report apart from other scholars. So whoever relates the report of the punishment of the Shade in a manner other than this manner which he related to us, then he has enjoined us to deny him, because he knew it and no one else knew it.

[p. 1065]

Allah, glorified is He, mentions the sixth of the stories of the prophets with their people, which is the story of Lut.

The *tafsīr* (exegesis) of His saying ﴿When he said to them﴾ up to His saying ﴿except for the Lord of the worlds﴾ has already passed in this surah. The *tafsīr* of the story of Lut has also already passed in full in al-A'raf, and so has His saying ﴿Do you approach males among the worlds?﴾. *Al-dhukrān* is the plural of *al-dhakar*, the opposite of the female. The meaning of *ta'tūna* is "you have intercourse with the males among the worlds." The "worlds" here are the children of Adam, or every living creature. They used to do this with strangers, as has already been mentioned in al-A'raf.

﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses﴾, that is, you abandon what Allah has created for your enjoyment of it among the women. By "spouses" He means the female sex in general. ﴿Rather, you are a people transgressing﴾, that is, exceeding the limit in all acts of disobedience, and this act you commit with males is among them.

﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Lut﴾ from forbidding us and denouncing our affair, ﴿you will surely be among those expelled﴾ from our land, those banished from it.

﴿He said, "Indeed, I am, of your deed﴾, which is what you are engaged in of mounting males, ﴿of those who detest it.﴾ *Al-qalī* is hatred. One says *qalaytuhu, aqlīhi, qalan wa qilā'an*. From this is the saying of the poet:

*"So I am not one whose companionship is hated, nor one who hates."*

And another said:

*"And what you have with me, if you are distant, is hatred."*

Then peace be upon him turned away from arguing with them and asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to save him, and he said: ﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do﴾, that is, from their wicked deed, or from the punishment that is about to befall them. So Allah, glorified is He, answered his supplication and said: ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them﴾, that is, the people of his household and whoever followed him in his religion and responded to his call.

﴿Except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾. She is the wife of Lut. The meaning of *min al-ghābirīn* is "among those who remained" in the punishment.

Abu Ubayda said: "among those who remained" means among those left behind in old age, that is, she remained until she became decrepit.

Al-Nahhas said: *ghābir* is said of the one who departs and of the one who remains.

The poet said:

*"Do not whip the she-camels' udders with their remaining milk, for you do not know who will be the one who gives birth."*

*Al-aghbār* are the remains of the milk. The Arabs say: *mā maḍā wa mā ghabar*, meaning "what has passed and what has remained."

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾, that is, We destroyed them by sinking and by stoning.

﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾, meaning stones, ﴿so evil was the rain of the warned.﴾ The thing praised or condemned is omitted, and the sense is "their rain."

The *tafsīr* of His saying ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾ and ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ has already passed in this surah.

﴿The companions of the thicket denied the messengers.﴾ Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read *Layka* with a single lam and an open ta', making it an indefinite noun not preceded by *al*, in apposition to (*aṣḥāb*) "companions." The rest read *al-Ayka* with the definite article. *Al-Ayka* is a dense growth of trees, that is, a thicket. *Layka* is a name for the town, and it was said that both have the same meaning, a name for the thicket.

Al-Qurtubi said: As for what Abu Ubayd related, that *Layka* is the name of the town in which they lived, and that *al-Ayka* is the name of the whole region, this is something that is not established, and no one who said it is known. Even if it were known, there would be room to question it, because the scholars all disagree with it.

Abu Ali al-Farisi said: *al-Ayka* is the definite form of *ayka*. When the hamza is dropped for lightness, its vowel is transferred to the lam.

Al-Khalil said: *al-Ayka* is a thicket that produces lote trees, acacia and similar soft trees.

﴿When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ He did not say "their brother," as he said of the prophets before him, because he was not from the companions of the thicket by lineage. When He mentioned Madyan, He said "their brother Shu'ayb," because he was from them. The verification of his lineage has already passed in al-A'raf. The *tafsīr* of His saying ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾ up to His saying, exalted is He, ﴿except for the Lord of the worlds﴾ has already passed in this surah.

His saying ﴿Give full measure and do not be among the shortchangers﴾: that is, complete the measure for whoever asks for it and deals with you by it. ﴿And do not be among the shortchangers﴾, those who diminish the measure and the weight. One says *akhsartu al-kayl wa al-wazn*, meaning "I diminished the measure and the weight." From this is His saying: ﴿And when they measure for them or weigh for them, they cause loss﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 3]. Then Allah, glorified is He, added further clarification and said: ﴿And weigh with an even balance﴾, that is, give the right with a sound scale. The explanation of this has already passed in the surah of Subhan (al-Isra'). It has been read as *bi-l-qusṭās* with a ḍamma and also with a kasra.

﴿And do not deprive people of their things﴾. *Al-bakhs* is diminution. One says *bakhasahu ḥaqqahu*, meaning "he diminished his right." That is, do not diminish people's rights that belong to them. This is a generalization after a specification. Its *tafsīr* has already passed in the surah of Hud. The *tafsīr* of His saying ﴿And do not commit abuse on the earth, causing corruption﴾ has also already passed, both in it and in other places.

﴿And fear Him who created you and the former generations.﴾ The majority read *al-jibilla* with a kasra on the jim and the ba' and a shadda on the lam. Abu Husayn, al-A'mash, al-Hasan, al-A'raj and Shayba read it with a ḍamma on both and a shadda on the lam. al-Sulami read it with a fatha on the jim and a sukun on the ba'. *Al-jibilla* means creation. This was said by Mujahid and others, meaning the earlier nations. One says *jubila fulān 'alā kadhā*, meaning "he was created with such and such."

Al-Nahhas said: creation is called *jibilla*, with a kasra on the first two letters, and also with a ḍamma on both with a shadda on the lam, and with a ḍamma on the jim and a sukun on the ba', with the ḍamma or fatha on it. Al-Harawi said: *al-jibilla*, *al-jubulla*, *al-jubl* and *al-jubal* are dialectal forms, and it means a large group of people with a great number. From this is His saying: ﴿a great multitude﴾ [Ya-Sin: 62], meaning a great creation. From this also is the saying of the poet:

*"Death is the greatest of events among what passes over the generations."*

﴿They said, "You are only of those bewitched, and you are not but a human like us.﴾ Its *tafsīr* has already been given in full in this surah. ﴿And indeed, we think you are among the liars.﴾ *In* here is the light form of the heavy one, and it governs a hidden pronoun of the matter. The lam is the distinguishing lam, meaning: concerning what you claim from us of messengerhood. It was also said that it is a negating *in*, and the lam has the meaning of *illā*, so that the sense is "we do not think you are among the liars." The first is preferred.

﴿So cause to fall upon us fragments from the sky﴾. Shu'ayb used to threaten them with punishment if they did not believe, so they said this to him as a challenge, as a way of making it seem unlikely and as a way of trying to incapacitate him. *Al-kisaf* is a piece. Abu Ubayda said: *al-kisaf* is the plural of *kisfa*, like *sidr* and *sidra*. Al-Jawhari said: *al-kisfa* is a piece of a thing. One says: "Give me a piece of your garment." Its plural is *kisaf*. The verification of this has already passed in the surah of Subhan.

﴿If you are of the truthful﴾ in your claim.

﴿He said, "My Lord is most knowing of what you do﴾ of polytheism and sins, so He will recompense you for that if He wills.﴾ In this is a severe threat.

[p. 1066] So they denied him, persisted in denying him, and insisted upon it. ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them.﴾ *Al-ẓulla* is the cloud. Allah raised it above their heads, and it rained fire upon them, and they perished. Allah afflicted them with what they had demanded, because if they meant by "fragments" a piece of the cloud, then it is clear, and if they meant by it a piece of the sky, then the punishment came down upon them from that direction. He attributed the punishment to the "Day of the Shade" and not to the shade itself, to alert that they had on that day a punishment other than the punishment of the shade. So it has been said.

Then Allah, glorified is He, described this punishment that befell them with His saying: ﴿Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾, because of the severity upon them, which cannot be measured.

The *tafsīr* of His saying ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾ and ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ has already passed in full in this surah, so we will not repeat it. In this repetition of these words at the end of these stories there is a threat, a rebuke, a confirmation and an emphasis that are not hidden from one who understands the placement of speech and knows its styles.

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses﴾, that he said: "You have left the fronts of women for the backs of men and the backs of women."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related the same from Ikrima.

They also related from Qatada, concerning ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾, that he said: "She is the wife of Lut, who remained in the punishment of Allah."

Abd ibn Humayd related from Mujahid, concerning *layka*, that he said: "It is al-Ayka."

Ishaq ibn Bishr and Ibn Asakir related from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿The companions of the thicket denied the messengers﴾, that he said: "They were the companions of a thicket on the shore of the sea, extending to Madyan." ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them﴾, and he did not say "their brother Shu'ayb," because he was not of their kind. ﴿Will you not fear Allah?﴾ How can you not fear Him, when you know that I am a trustworthy messenger? Will you not take heed from the destruction of Madyan, who were destroyed for what they used to do? The companions of the thicket, despite what they were in of polytheism, followed the custom of the companions of Madyan. So Shu'ayb said to them: "Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. I do not ask you for any reward for what I call you to in this world from your wealth. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds. And fear Him who created you and the former generations," meaning the earlier generations who were destroyed for their sins, "and do not perish like them." ﴿They said, "You are only of those bewitched"﴾, meaning of the created beings. ﴿And you are not but a human like us, and indeed we think you are among the liars. So cause to fall upon us fragments from the sky﴾, meaning pieces from the sky. ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them.﴾ Allah sent against them scorching winds from Hell, and they surrounded them for seven days until the heat cooked them. Their houses became hot, and their water boiled in the wells and springs. So they left their dwellings and their settlements, fleeing, and the scorching wind was with them. Allah then made the sun dominant over them from above their heads, and it covered them until their skulls rattled within it. And Allah made the hot sand dominant beneath their feet until the flesh of their feet fell away. Then a shade like a black cloud arose for them. When they saw it, they rushed to seek refuge in its shade. When all of them were gathered beneath it, it closed over them, and they perished. Allah saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him, saying concerning ﴿and the former generations﴾: "the earlier creations."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim also related from him that he was asked about His saying ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them.﴾ He said: "Allah sent upon them an intense heat that seized their breaths, so they entered the inner parts of the houses, but it entered upon them within the houses and seized their souls. So they came out of the houses fleeing into the wilderness. Then Allah sent upon them a cloud that shaded them from the sun, and they found in it coolness and pleasure. So they called to one another until, when they had gathered beneath it, Allah rained fire upon them. That is the punishment of the Day of the Shade."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim also related from him: "Whoever relates to you from the scholars the punishment of the Day of the Shade, then deny him."

I say: What can we say concerning what he (may Allah be pleased with him) related to us of that, which we have transmitted from him here? It may be said that since he was the sea whom Allah taught the interpretation of His Book through the supplication of His Prophet (may Allah bless him, his family and grant him peace), he was singled out for knowledge of this report apart from other scholars. So whoever relates the report of the punishment of the Shade in a manner other than this manner which he related to us, then he has enjoined us to deny him, because he knew it and no one else knew it.

al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, on Surah 26, verses 214–227 (part 1 of 3)

[p. 1067] His words: ﴿And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾. The pronoun refers to what He sent down to him of the reports (akhbar): that is, "and indeed these reports," or "and indeed the Qur'an," although it has not been mentioned before, since it is known. It has been said that this is on the assumption of an omitted genitive construction (mudaf mahdhuf), meaning "possessor of a revelation." But if tanzil is taken in the sense of munazzal (that which is sent down), there is no need to assume an omitted genitive construction.

Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Hafs from 'Asim read *nazala* with a light (unshaddened) form, and the rest read it with a shadda (*nazzala*). In the second reading, ﴿the Trustworthy Spirit﴾ is in the accusative as the direct object. Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading. The Trustworthy Spirit is Gabriel, as in His words: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, for he has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [al-Baqarah: 97].

The meaning of ﴿upon your heart﴾ is that he recited it to his heart. The reason for specifying the heart is that it is the first of the inner senses to perceive.

Abu Hayyan said: ﴿upon your heart﴾ and ﴿that you may be among the warners﴾ are both connected to *nazala* (the verb "sent down"). It has been said that they may be connected to *tanzil* (revelation). The first is preferable. It has also been read as *nuzzila* (with shadda, in the passive voice), with God, exalted is He, as the agent, and in this reading the Spirit is in the nominative as the deputy of the agent (na'ib al-fa'il).

﴿That you may be among the warners﴾ is the reason (illah) for the sending down: that is, He sent it down so that you might warn them with what it contains of cautions, warnings and punishments.

﴿In a clear Arabic tongue﴾ is connected to "the warners," meaning: that you may be among the warners in this tongue. Abu al-Baqa' permitted that it be an apposition (badal) for "it." It has also been said that it is connected to *nazala*. It was placed later for emphasis on the mention of warning. God, glorified is He, made the Qur'an Arabic in the tongue of the Arab Messenger so that the idolaters of the Arabs would not say, "We do not understand what you say, other than in our own tongue." Thus He cut off their argument, removed their excuse, and rejected their pretext.

﴿And indeed it is in the scriptures of the earlier peoples﴾: that is, this Qur'an, in respect of its rulings on which the revealed laws agree, is in the books of the earlier prophets. The *zubur* (scriptures) are the books; the singular is *zabur*. The discussion of the interpretation of similar expressions has already passed.

It has been said that the pronoun refers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace. It has also been said that what is meant by the Qur'an being in the scriptures of the earlier peoples is that it is itself mentioned in them, not merely that they contain its rulings. The first is preferable.

﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ The interrogative hamza is for denial (inkar), and the waw is for conjunction with an implied preceding clause, as has been mentioned many times. A *ayah* is a sign and an indication. That is: is there not for these people a sign indicating that the Qur'an is true, that it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, and that it is in the scriptures of the earlier peoples, that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it generally, or those among them who believed, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam? The testimony of the People of the Book became a proof against the idolaters because they used to refer to them and accept their word.

Ibn 'Amir read *takun* with the feminine ending (ta' fawqiyyah, i.e. the verb as feminine), and *ayatun* in the nominative, making it the subject of *kana*, with its predicate being ﴿that they know it﴾ and so on. It may also be a complete verb (taamma, "to occur/exist"). The rest read *yakun* with the masculine (ya' tahtiyyah), and *ayatan* in the accusative, making it the predicate of *yakun*, with its subject being ﴿that they know it﴾ and so on.

al-Zajjaj said: "*an ya'lamahu*" is the subject of *yakun*, and "*ayatan*" is its predicate.

The meaning is: or was it not a sign and indication to them, that the knowledge of the scholars of the Children of Israel, that Muhammad is a true prophet, is a sign and proof of his prophethood? For the scholars among the Children of Israel who believed used to inform people that his mention existed in their books. So also said al-Farra', and the justification for the reading with the nominative is what we have mentioned.

As for Ibn 'Amir's reading, there is a problem with it, because making an indefinite noun the subject and a definite noun the predicate is not permissible, even though it occurs irregularly in such lines as the poet's:

*fa-la yakun mawqifun minka al-wada'a*
(So let there not be, from you, a standing-place of farewell)

and the other's:

*wa-kana mizajuha 'asalun wa-ma'*
(And its mixture was honey and water)

There is no basis for what has been said, that the indefinite noun became specific through their saying *lahum* ("for them"), because it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), and a circumstantial clause is descriptive in meaning. The best justification to give is what we have already mentioned, that *yakun* is complete.

﴿And had We sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾: that is, had We sent the Qur'an in the form it is in, upon a man from the non-Arabs who cannot speak in Arabic.

﴿And he had recited it to them﴾ a correct recitation, ﴿they would not have believed in it﴾, with the added miracle of the recitation coming from the non-Arab man of the Arabic speech, to the miracle of the Qur'an.

It has also been said that the meaning is: had We sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs in the tongue of the non-Arabs, and he had recited it to them in their language, they would not have believed in it, and they would have said, "We do not comprehend this and do not understand it." A similar statement is His words: ﴿And had We made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail?"﴾ [Fussilat: 44]. It is said: *rajul a'jam* and *a'jami* for a man who is not eloquent in speech even if he is an Arab; and *rajul 'ajami* for a man whose origin is from the non-Arabs even if he is eloquent. However, al-Farra' permitted saying *rajul 'ajami* in the sense of *a'jami*.

al-Hasan read *'ala ba'di al-a'jamiyyin* ("upon some of the non-Arabs" with the full *-iyyin* ending), and similarly al-Jahdari read it.

Abu al-Fath ibn Jinni said: the original form of *al-a'jamin* is *al-a'jamiyyin*, then the *ya'* of the relative (nisba) was dropped, and its plural with the *ya'* and *nun* was made to indicate it.

﴿Thus We have caused it to enter the hearts of the criminals﴾: that is, in the same manner We have made it enter, meaning: We have caused it to enter their hearts, that is, the Qur'an, until they understood its meanings, recognized its eloquence, and knew that it is inimitable.

al-Hasan and others said: We caused polytheism and denial to enter the hearts of the criminals.

Ikrimah said: We caused hardness (qaswah) to enter. The first is preferable, because the context is about the Qur'an. The clause ﴿they do not believe﴾ may bear two interpretations. The first is that it is a resumed clause (isti'naf), giving clarification and explanation of what precedes it. The second is that it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in *salaknahu* ("We caused it to enter"). It may also be a circumstantial clause from "the criminals."

al-Farra' permitted the jussive mood (jazm) in *la yu'minun* ("they do not believe"), because it carries the sense of a condition and consequence. He claimed that it is among the habits of the Arabs that when they place *la* in the position of *kay la* (in order that not), as in this case, they sometimes put the following verb in the jussive and sometimes in the nominative. So they say: *rabatu al-faras la yanfalit* ("I tied the horse so it would not escape"), with nominative and jussive both, because its meaning is: "if I do not tie it, it will escape." He cited for the nominative a line from one of the Banu 'Uqayl:

*wa-hatta ra'ayna ahsana al-fi'li baynana * masakinahu la yaqrubu al-sharra qarib*
(Until we saw the finest of deeds among us, its dwellings, no one who approaches evil approaches)

And for the jussive, another's line:

*la-talama ma halaltumaha la tarid * fakhalliyaha wal-sikhalu tabtarid*
(How often you have halted her, so do not come to water; so leave her, while the young camels cool themselves)

al-Nahhas said: all of this regarding *la yu'minun* is an error according to the Basran grammarians, and it is not permitted to jussify without a jussifying particle.

﴿Until they see the painful punishment﴾: that is, they do not believe up to this limit, which is their witnessing of the painful punishment.

﴿So it will come upon them suddenly﴾: that is, abruptly, suddenly, ﴿while they perceive not﴾ its coming. al-Hasan read *fa-ta'tiyahum* with the feminine ta' (fawqiyyah), meaning: the Hour, even though it has not been mentioned before; but it indicates the punishment, and so the Hour is implied by it.

﴿Then they will say: "Are we to be reprieved?"﴾: that is, are we to be delayed and given respite?

They said this in regret for what they had missed of faith, and in longing for a return to the world to make up for what they had neglected.

It has also been said that what is meant by their saying ﴿Are we to be reprieved?﴾ is a demand to hasten the punishment, in the manner of mockery. This is supported by His words: [p. 1068] ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾. But the distance and contradiction with the apparent meaning in this are not hidden, for the meaning of ﴿Are we to be reprieved?﴾ is a request for respite and delay. As for His words ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾, the intended meaning is refutation and denial of what they had said: ﴿Rain down upon us stones from heaven, or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 32], and their saying ﴿Bring us what you threaten us with﴾ [al-A'raf: 70; Hud: 32; al-Ahqaf: 22].

﴿Have you considered: if We let them enjoy for years﴾: the interrogative is for denial, and the fa' is for conjunction with an implied preceding clause suitable to the context, as has passed in more than one place. The meaning of *ara'ayta* is "tell me," and the address is to everyone who is fit for it. That is: tell me, if We let them enjoy the world for long years, and extended their lifespans.

﴿Then there comes to them what they were promised﴾ of the punishment and destruction.

﴿Of no avail to them will be what they had been enjoying﴾. *Ma* here is the interrogative: the meaning is, what thing will avail them their being given that long enjoyment? The *ma* in ﴿what they were enjoying﴾ may be the verbal-masdar *ma* (meaning "that which they were enjoying" or "their enjoying"), and it may be the relative *ma*. The interrogative is for emphatic denial (inkar taqriri). The first *ma* may also be a negative, with the object omitted, meaning: their enjoyment did not avail them anything. It was read as *yumta'un* (with the ya' prefix and the hamza in the verb form of *amta'a*) with the *mim* sukun and the *ta'* lightened, from *amta'a Allahu Zaydan bi-kadha* (God gave Zayd enjoyment with such-and-such).

﴿And We never destroyed a town but it had warners﴾: *min* is extra for emphasis, meaning: We did not destroy any town of the towns except that it had warners.

The clause ﴿but it had warners﴾ may be a descriptive clause of *qaryah* ("town"), and it may be a circumstantial clause from it. The denial preceding it permits this. The meaning is: We did not destroy a town of the towns except after warning them and giving them an excuse by sending messengers and sending down books.

His words ﴿a reminder﴾ mean "a reminder," and it is in the accusative position as a reason (illah) or as an infinitive (masdar).

al-Kisa'i said: *dhikra* is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause.

al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: it is in the accusative position as an infinitive, meaning: they remind (*yadhkurun dhikra*).

al-Nahhas said: this is a correct opinion, because the meaning of ﴿but it had warners﴾ is "but it had reminders."

al-Zajjaj said: *dhikra* may also be in the nominative position, as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: our warning is a reminder, or: that is a reminder.

Ibn al-Anbari said: the meaning is "it is a reminder," or "it reminds them as a reminder." al-Akhfash preferred that it is the predicate of an omitted subject.

﴿And We were not unjust﴾ in punishing them, for We had already presented the proof to them, warned them, and given them an excuse.

﴿And the devils did not bring it down﴾: that is, the Qur'an. This is a rejection of what the disbelievers claimed about the Qur'an, that it is among what the devils cast upon the soothsayers.

﴿And it is not becoming for them﴾ to do that, nor is it valid from them, ﴿nor are they able﴾ to do what the disbelievers attributed to them at all.

﴿Indeed they are removed from hearing﴾ the Qur'an, or the speech of the angels, ﴿and are barred﴾: that is, veiled, stoned with meteors.

al-Hasan, Ibn al-Sumayfa' and al-A'mash read *ma tanazzalat bihi al-shayatinu* with the plural masculine ending (waw and nun), treating it as a sound masculine plural (*ijra'an lahu majra al-salama*). al-Nahhas said: this is an error according to all the grammarians. He said: I heard 'Ali ibn Sulayman say: I heard Muhammad ibn Yazid say: this is one of the errors of the scholars, and it arose from a confusion: al-Hasan saw at the end of it a *ya'* and *nun*, and since it is in the nominative position, it was confused with the sound masculine plural, and so he erred.

al-Farra' said: "The shaykh erred," meaning al-Hasan. It was said this to al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, and he said: If it is permissible to cite the verses of Ru'bah and al-'Ajjaj and their like, then it is permissible to cite the reading of al-Hasan and his companion, meaning Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa'; besides, we know that they would not have read it that way unless they had heard something about it.

al-Mu'arrij said: if *al-shaytan* is derived from *shaṭa yashiṭu*, then their reading has a basis.

Yunus ibn Habib said: I heard a Bedouin say: "We entered gardens, and behind them were other gardens."

Then, when He, glorified is He, had established the truth of the Qur'an and that it was sent down from Him, He commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, to call upon God alone, saying: ﴿So do not call upon another god along with God, or you will be among those punished﴾. The address to the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, with this, though he is exempt from it and protected from it, is to urge the servants toward monotheism and to forbid them the admixture of polytheism. It is as if He said: you are the most honored of creation to Me and the dearest to Me; if you were to take another god with Me, I would punish you. So how much more would this be the case for others among the servants?

﴿And warn your nearest kindred﴾: He specified the nearest because concern for them is more fitting, and guiding them to the truth is more urgent.

It has been said they are the Quraysh; it has also been said they are the Banu 'Abd Manaf; it has also been said they are the Banu Hashim.

It is firmly established in the Sahih that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) summoned the Quraysh, and they gathered. He addressed them both in general and in particular. This was his explanation (ﷺ) that the verse referred to the closest kinsfolk, and the details of that will come later.

﴿And lower your wing to the believers who follow you.﴾ It is said: "He lowered his wing" when he was gentle toward someone, and there is a fine *isti'ara* (metaphor, a figurative usage) here.

The meaning: be gentle and humble toward those among the believers who follow you, show them affection and honour, and overlook their faults.

﴿But if they disobey you﴾, that is, they oppose your command and do not follow you, ﴿then say: "I am innocent of what you do."﴾ That is, of your deeds, or of what you are doing. This indicates that the "believers" here are those who are close to faith and affirm it with their tongues, since true believers do not disobey him or oppose him.

Then He explained to him what he should rely upon when they disobeyed him, saying: ﴿And put your trust in the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ That is, entrust your affairs to Him, for He is able to subdue the enemies, and He is merciful to the allies.

Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read *fa-tawakkal* with the *fa'* (so, therefore). The rest read *wa-tawakkal* with the *waw* (and). According to the first reading, what follows the *fa'* is like a part of what precedes it, consequent upon it. According to the second reading, what follows the *waw* is coordinated with what precedes it as a sentence joined to a sentence, without a sequential order.

﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾, that is, when you stand for prayer alone, according to the view of most exegetes.

Mujahid said: "When you stand," wherever you are.

﴿And your movements among those who prostrate﴾, that is, He sees you when you pray in congregation, bowing and prostrating and standing. So said most exegetes.

It was also said: He sees you among the monotheists, from prophet to prophet, until He brought you forth in this community.

It was also said: the meaning of His words "who sees you when you stand" is His seeing your standing for the night prayer (*tahajjud*). And His words "your movements among those who prostrate" mean your roaming and scanning through the states of those who strive in worship, and the turning of your gaze upon them. So said Mujahid.

﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾ of what you say, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of it.

Then He, glorified is He, emphasised and clarified the meaning of His words: ﴿And the devils have not brought it down﴾, saying: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ That is, upon whom they descend, with one of the two *ta'*s dropped. In this there is a demonstration that it is impossible for the devils to descend upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

﴿They descend upon every lying sinner.﴾ *Affak* means one who fabricates much, and *athim* means one who commits much sin. The intended meaning is every person who was a soothsayer (*kahin*), for the devils used to eavesdrop on the heavens, then came to them and conveyed what they had heard.

This is the meaning of His words: ﴿They cast the hearing﴾, that is, what they hear of what they eavesdrop. On this reading, the clause ﴿they cast the hearing﴾ refers to the devils and is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: while the devils are casting the hearing, that is, what they hear from the higher assembly (the angels) to the soothsayers.

It is also permissible that the meaning is: the devils cast the hearing, that is, they listen attentively to the higher assembly in order to snatch something from them. On the first reading, "the hearing" means what is heard; on the second reading, it means the faculty of hearing itself.

It is also permissible that the clause ﴿they cast the hearing﴾ refers to every lying sinner, either as a description or as a new, independent sentence. The meaning of "casting" is that they hear what the devils convey to them of words, of which one in a hundred is true and a hundred are false, as is reported in the hadith.

The clause ﴿and most of them are liars﴾ refers to ﴿every lying sinner﴾. That is, most of these soothsayers are liars in what they receive from the devils, because they add to what they hear many of their various falsehoods. Or: most of them are liars in what they cast of the hearing, that is, what is heard from the devils and passed on to people. It is also permissible that the clause ﴿and most of them are liars﴾ refers to the devils, that is, most of the devils are liars in what they convey to the soothsayers of what they hear, for they add much falsehood of their own to it.

It has been asked: how is it sound, on the first reading, to describe the fabricators as "most of them are liars," after they have all been described as fabricators? It is answered that the intended meaning of "fabricator" is one who abounds in lying, not one who speaks nothing but lies. So the meaning of "most of them are liars" is that few of them speak the truth in what they relate about the devils. The purpose for which this discourse came is to refute what the polytheists claimed, namely that the Prophet (ﷺ) was among those to whom the devil casts the hearing from the soothsayers. This is shown by making clear that the overwhelming characteristic of soothsayers is lying, whereas nothing has appeared from the states of Muhammad (ﷺ) except truthfulness. How, then, could he be as they claimed? Furthermore, these soothsayers exalt the devils, while this Messenger sent from God, with his message to people, censures them, curses them, and commands seeking refuge from them. Then, since one of the polytheists had said that the Prophet (ﷺ) was a poet, God, glorified is He, described the state of poets and the incompatibility of what they are upon with what the Prophet (ﷺ) is upon, saying: ﴿And the poets, the misguided follow them.﴾ The meaning: the poets are followed by those who keep pace with them, follow their path, and are among them, the misguided, that is, those who have strayed from the truth. *Shu'ara'* is the plural of *sha'ir* (poet), and *ghawun* is the plural of *ghawin* (one who goes astray). They are the misguided among the jinn and mankind.

It was said: they are those who turn away from the truth. It was said: they are those who transmit poetry containing satire and what is impermissible. It was said: the intended meaning is specifically the poets of the disbelievers.

The majority read *wa-ash-shu'ara'u* with the *damma* (nominative), as a subject whose predicate is what follows. 'Isa ibn 'Umar read *ash-shu'ara'a* with the *fatha* (accusative), as the *ishtighal* construction (a verb governing an accusative by implication). Nafi', Shayba, al-Hasan and al-Sulami read *yatba'uhum* with a single *ta'* (lightened), and the rest read it with a doubled *ta'* (intensified).

Then God, glorified is He, mentioned the vices of the poets of falsehood, saying: ﴿Have you not seen that they wander in every valley?﴾ The sentence confirms what precedes it, and the address is to everyone who is capable of seeing. It is said: "*hama yahimu haymana wa-haymanan*" when one goes off in a direction without aim. That is: have you not seen that they plunge into every kind of falsehood, and speak in every ravine of deceit?
